_note: Claim Adjustment Reason Codes (CARC) and Remittance Advice Remark Codes (RARC),
as they appear on an 835 remittance. Two different things live in each entry and
'description' is the published meaning of the code. Do not edit it to taste --
it is what the payer is actually saying.
'category' is RUBY'S judgement about what kind of problem this is, which drives
the recommended route (correct the codes, appeal with documentation, bill the
patient, and so on). This one is ours to tune as real denials teach us more.
This list is deliberately partial -- the most common codes, not the full set.
An unrecognised code is reported raw and categorised 'unknown' rather than
guessed at, the same discipline the ICD-10 loader uses: a confident wrong
explanation about money is worse than an honest 'we don't know this one'.
The full CARC/RARC lists are maintained by Washington Publishing Company.
Check redistribution terms before shipping a complete set commercially -- this
is potentially the same shape of problem as the open CPT licensing question.

CO.name: Contractual Obligation
CO.meaning: The provider absorbs this amount under the payer contract. It cannot be billed to the patient.

PR.name: Patient Responsibility
PR.meaning: The patient owes this amount -- deductible, coinsurance, or copay.

OA.name: Other Adjustment
OA.meaning: Neither a contractual write-off nor patient responsibility. Usually coordination of benefits.

PI.name: Payer Initiated Reduction
PI.meaning: The payer reduced payment on its own initiative, not under the contract. Often appealable.
